newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on consolidation.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed Saturday's half-day session slightly lower on consolidation following recent gains, brokers said.
But strong buying interest remained strong among theme-backed smaller-capitalised shares.
The composite stock index lost 1.03 points to 767.27.
"The market continued its consolidation," said Koh Soon-sik at LG Securities. "With no favourable news, the market will fall further. But I don't expect any sharp declines on the index."
Brokers forecast the index would move in a boxed range between 750 and 770 next week.
Blue chips spearheaded the decline as investors tended to shun those shares with no signs of an economic turnaround in sight, brokers said.
Both Samsung Electronics and steelmaker POSCO fell 400 won to 67,600 and 62,800, respectively.
The consolidation also hit financial shares hard as its sub-index lost 5.80 points, or 1.02 percent, to 563.43.
But some smaller-cap companies continued to come under the spotlight. Investors believed they could gain profits in those shares given the current level of market energy, brokers said.

Leading door-lock maker Hyundai Metal rose to its daily upper limit, gaining 1,100 won to 15,300 with heavy trading volume of 271,850. Construction material producer Kum Kang also rose to upper limit of 900 won to 12,300.
"Small-cap shares seemed to be overheated. They will face profit-taking next week," said a Daewoo Securities broker. He said blue chips would stage a brief technical rebound next week.
